correctness.rationale: The wheel automorphism orbits are hub–rim and two-rim cyclic distances. Hub–rim grounding leaves a tridiagonal path T_(n−1)=3I−A(P), giving the eigenvalue sum. Two-rim grounding gives two path blocks and a central hub Schur complement; the squared inverse Frobenius norm yields an exact rational orbit cost. Direct independent Laplacian-matrix inversion across all labeled leader pairs for 3≤n≤10 recovers winner counts 6,2,5,n and the W6 objective reversal. For n≥11, a follower all-ones Rayleigh test bounds λ_min≤6/(n−1), so two-rim J2≥(n−1)²/36. The infinite-path positive Green kernel bounds the hub–rim inverse squared norm by 3(n−1)/(5sqrt(5)); since 3/(5sqrt5)<27/100<10/36 and n−1≥10 this is strictly smaller. Hence bounded cases plus the uniform tail prove all sizes. The second-order relative-damping modal Lyapunov normalization yields positional variance J2/(2η); it does not cover other damping/noise models.

final_claim: For an unweighted wheel with n≥3 rim vertices and exactly two noise-free grounded leaders, minimizing trace(L_FF^−2) selects all pairs at n=3, opposite rim pairs at n=4, distance-two rim pairs at n=5, and exactly hub–rim pairs for n≥6, with sharp exact minima and a first-inverse/inverse-square preference reversal on W6.
